142	        parse_metrics('{"x": Infinity}')
143	    except ValueError:
144	        pass
145	    else:
146	        raise AssertionError("expected ValueError for Infinity literal")
147	
148	
149	def _record(path, line):
150	    append_metrics(path, line)
151	    return 0
152	
153	
154	def _recover(path):
155	    # One canonical JSON line per recovered record, exit 0 afterwards.
156	    for metrics in recover_metrics(path):
157	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
158	    return 0
159	
160	
161	def _rotate(path):
162	    rotate_metrics(path)
163	    return 0
164	
165	
166	def _stream(path):
167	    # Records stream straight to stdout one JSON object per line; the
168	    # segment set is never materialised in memory.
169	    for metrics in iter_metrics(path):
170	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
171	    return 0
172	
173	
174	def _compact(path):
175	    compact_metrics(path)
176	    return 0
177	
178	
179	def _prune(path, quota):
180	    prune_metrics(path, quota)
181	    return 0
182	
183	
184	def _resume(path, position):
185	    # Like stream, starting at the record position; a position that does
186	    # not parse as an integer is a usage error handled in main().
187	    for metrics in resume_metrics(path, position):
188	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
189	    return 0
190	
191	
192	def _snapshot(path):
193	    # Pin the current record sequence and print the persistable handle.
194	    sys.stdout.write(snapshot_metrics(path) + "\n")
195	    return 0
196	
197	
198	def _release(path, handle):
199	    release_metrics(path, handle)
200	    return 0
201	
202	
203	def _snap_resume(path, handle, position):
204	    # Stream the snapshot pinned by handle from the record position; a
205	    # position that does not parse as an integer is a usage error.
206	    for metrics in resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position):
207	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
208	    return 0
209	
210	
211	def _snap_diff(path, old_handle, new_handle):
212	    # Each difference is already a complete newline-terminated JSON
213	    # line with keys in the fixed kind/position/old/new order; write it
214	    # verbatim so pinned bytes and key order are not re-rendered.
215	    for line in snapshot_diff_metrics(path, old_handle, new_handle):
216	        sys.stdout.write(line)
217	    return 0
218	
219	
220	def _snap_cursor(path, handle, position):
221	    # Stream not-yet-read live records from the record position; a
222	    # position that does not parse as an integer is a usage error.
223	    for metrics in resume_snapshot_delta_metrics(path, handle, position):
224	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
225	    return 0
226	
227	
228	def _checkpoint(path, handle, cursor_path, position):
229	    # Persist the pull cursor (position, handle and record boundary) to
230	    # the caller-named cursor file; a position that does not parse as an
231	    # integer is a usage error handled in main().
232	    checkpoint_metrics(path, handle, cursor_path, position)
233	    return 0
234	
235	
236	def _cursor_resume(path, cursor_path):
237	    # Stream the pinned snapshot onward from the stored cursor position,
238	    # one canonical JSON object per record.
239	    for metrics in resume_checkpoint_metrics(path, cursor_path):
240	        sys.stdout.write(render_metrics(metrics))
241	    return 0
242	
243	
244	def _group_checkpoint(path, cursor_paths, positions):
245	    # Advance the whole group of cursors in one atomic commit; positions
246	    # that do not parse as integers are usage errors handled in main().
247	    checkpoint_group_metrics(path, cursor_paths, positions)
248	    return 0
249	
250	
251	def _replay(path, cursor_path, start, end):
252	    # Stream the window one compact JSON object per line: metric records
253	    # and gap markers (a gap marker is not a metric, so items are
254	    # rendered directly rather than through render_metrics).
255	    for item in replay_metrics(path, cursor_path, start, end):
256	        sys.stdout.write(
257	            json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
258	        )
259	    return 0
260	
261	
262	def _group_pairs(rest):
263	    """Parse the group-checkpoint cursor/position arguments into pairs.
264	
265	    Positions are the arguments that parse as integers.  Alternating
266	    ``CURSOR POSITION`` pairs, alternating ``POSITION CURSOR`` pairs and
267	    all cursor files followed by all positions are all accepted; a
268	    position that does not parse as an integer or a leftover argument
269	    count makes the whole form a usage error (``None``).
270	    """
271	    def _is_int(text):
272	        try:
273	            int(text)
274	        except ValueError:
275	            return False
276	        return True
277	
278	    if not rest or len(rest) % 2 != 0:
279	        return None
280	    if all(
281	        not _is_int(rest[i]) and _is_int(rest[i + 1])
282	        for i in range(0, len(rest), 2)
283	    ):
284	        return [(rest[i], int(rest[i + 1])) for i in range(0, len(rest), 2)]
285	    if all(
286	        _is_int(rest[i]) and not _is_int(rest[i + 1])
287	        for i in range(0, len(rest), 2)
288	    ):
289	        return [(rest[i + 1], int(rest[i])) for i in range(0, len(rest), 2)]
290	    half = len(rest) // 2
291	    cursors, numbers = rest[:half], rest[half:]
292	    if all(not _is_int(text) for text in cursors) and all(
293	        _is_int(text) for text in numbers
294	    ):
295	        return list(zip(cursors, [int(text) for text in numbers]))
296	    return None
297	
298	
299	def _dispatch(handler, path):
300	    # rotate/stream failures are reported cleanly and end with status 1.
301	    try:
302	        return handler(path)
303	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
304	        print(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
305	        return 1
306	
307	
308	def main(argv=None):
309	    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
310	    if args == ["--selftest"]:
311	        _selftest()
312	        print("selftest ok")
313	        return 0
314	    if args and args[0] == "record":
315	        if len(args) != 3:

319	    if args and args[0] == "recover":

329	    if args and args[0] == "stream":

334	    if args and args[0] == "compact":
335	        if len(args) != 2:
336	            print(_USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
337	            return 2
338	        return _dispatch(_compact, args[1])
339	    if args and args[0] == "resume":
340	        if len(args) not in (2, 3):

344	        if len(args) == 3:

351	    if args and args[0] == "prune":

356	            quota = int(args[2])

371	    if args and args[0] == "snap-resume":
372	        if len(args) not in (3, 4):

1	# weighted-batcher
2	
3	Weighted sampling helpers whose selection sequence is reproducible from a seed, plus metric rendering that keeps very large counters exact.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m weighted_batcher --selftest
16	
17	Append one metric line to a durable log, recover the log back as JSON, seal it into a numbered segment, stream it back, compact every segment into one, or resume reading at a saved position:
18	
19	    python3 -m weighted_batcher record FILE METRICS_JSON
20	    python3 -m weighted_batcher recover FILE
21	    python3 -m weighted_batcher rotate FILE
22	    python3 -m weighted_batcher stream FILE
23	    python3 -m weighted_batcher compact FILE
24	    python3 -m weighted_batcher resume FILE [POSITION]
25	    python3 -m weighted_batcher prune FILE QUOTA
26	    python3 -m weighted_batcher snapshot FILE
27	    python3 -m weighted_batcher release FILE HANDLE
28	    python3 -m weighted_batcher snap-resume FILE HANDLE [POSITION]
29	
30	`recover` and `stream` print one JSON object per line on stdout and exit 0.
31	`rotate` seals `FILE` into a numbered segment (`FILE.1`, then one past the
32	highest number already present), leaving an empty `FILE` behind, and exits 0.
33	`compact` merges every segment and the current log into `FILE.1`, leaving an
34	empty `FILE` behind; an empty log set still produces an empty `FILE.1`.
35	`resume` prints records from `POSITION` (the number of records already read
36	from the start in write order, default 0) onward; the position stays valid
37	across appends, rotations, compactions and pruning. `prune` retains at most
38	`QUOTA` records, dropping the oldest whole records; `QUOTA` 0 drops every
39	record. Pruned records keep their write-order positions, so a `POSITION`
40	inside or at the prune point reads from the oldest surviving record, and
41	only a position past the total record count (pruned included) is out of
42	range. `snapshot` pins the complete record sequence at creation time and
43	prints a persistable handle; `snap-resume` streams the pinned sequence
44	from `POSITION` (same ordinal rules as `resume`, default 0), and
45	`release` retires the handle. `rotate`, `stream`, `compact`, `resume`,
46	`prune`, `snapshot`, `release` and `snap-resume` exit 1 on
47	failure; wrong argument counts and a `POSITION` or `QUOTA` that is not an
48	integer print usage on stderr and exit 2.
49	
50	## Public interface
51	
52	`weighted_batcher.Sampler(weights, replacement=True, seed=None)`.
53	- `Sampler.sample(n) -> list[int]` returns drawn indices.
54	- In without-replacement mode draws accumulate on the instance: repeated
55	  `sample` calls never return an index already drawn, and requesting more
56	  draws than the remaining positive-weight items raises `ValueError`.
57	- `Sampler.weights -> list[float]` as supplied.
58	- `weighted_batcher.render_metrics(metrics) -> str` returns one line of JSON.
59	- `weighted_batcher.parse_metrics(line) -> dict` accepts what `render_metrics` produced.
60	- `weighted_batcher.append_metrics(path, line) -> None` validates one JSON object
61	  line and appends it to `path`. Concurrent processes appending to the same file
62	  never interleave records. Raises `OSError` if `line` is not a string or the
63	  path is not writable, `ValueError` if the top level is not a JSON object, and
64	  `TypeError` if a key is not a string or a value is not an int or float
65	  (booleans do not count).
66	- `weighted_batcher.recover_metrics(path) -> list[dict]` reads the log set
67	  back: segments `path.1`, `path.2`, ... in ascending order followed by the
68	  current log at `path`. Every complete newline-terminated line is parsed; a
69	  torn unterminated tail left by a crashed writer is silently discarded.
70	  Blank lines (`\n` and `\r\n`) are skipped. A non-JSON complete line raises
71	  `ValueError` naming its file and line number. An empty or newline-only file
72	  yields `[]`. Missing files raise `FileNotFoundError` (only when neither the
73	  current log nor any segment exists); directories raise
74	  `IsADirectoryError`. Large counters return as exact ints, `-0.0` is
75	  preserved, and key order follows the file.
76	- `weighted_batcher.rotate_metrics(path) -> None` seals the current log into
77	  the next numbered segment (`path.1`, then one past the greatest number
78	  already present, so a deleted number is never reused) and leaves an empty
79	  file at `path`; an empty log seals an empty segment. Concurrent appenders
80	  are serialised with a file lock, so every accepted record lands in exactly
81	  one segment or in the current log. A crash after sealing but before
82	  re-creation still leaves the segment readable in write order. Raises
83	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
84	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking failure.
85	- `weighted_batcher.iter_metrics(path)` is the streaming counterpart of
86	  `recover_metrics`: it yields records line by line across segments and the
87	  current log without loading them into memory, with the same parsing and
88	  error semantics.
89	- `weighted_batcher.compact_metrics(path) -> None` merges all segments and
90	  the current log into the single fixed segment `path.1` and leaves the
91	  current log empty; a completely empty set still yields an empty segment.
92	  Complete records are copied byte for byte with their original newlines —
93	  not re-rendered, de-duplicated or reordered, so `-0.0`, oversized counters
94	  and key order are preserved; torn tails are dropped and blank lines
95	  skipped just like on read. The merge is fully written and flushed to a
96	  temporary file before being atomically published as `path.compact`, and
97	  only then are old segments removed and the result renamed to `path.1`;
98	  a half-written crash leftover never joins recovery, and while staging
99	  exists recovery and streaming read only it. A later append, rotation or
100	  compaction transparently finishes an interrupted cleanup. Raises
101	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
102	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write failure.
103	- `weighted_batcher.resume_metrics(path, position=0)` streams records from
104	  `position` onward, where `position` is the number of records already read
105	  from the start of the segment set in write order. The position needs no
106	  conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
107	  cleanup, and is only out of range when it exceeds the record total
108	  (pruned records included); equal to the total the stream is empty.
109	  Reading stays line by line and linear, never materialising the segment
110	  set. Raises `TypeError` if `position` is not an integer (booleans do not
111	  count), `ValueError` for a negative or out-of-range position (the latter
112	  while iterating), with the same path and line-level errors as
113	  `iter_metrics`.
114	- `weighted_batcher.prune_metrics(path, quota)` keeps at most `quota`
115	  records, dropping whole records from the oldest end in write order;
116	  `quota` 0 drops every record, and a quota at or above the current count
117	  removes nothing. A record is never split, empty and torn-tail-only
118	  segments spend no quota, and survivors keep their bytes, order,
119	  newlines, `-0.0`, oversized counters and key order. The set remembers
120	  the number of records pruned (`path.prune`), so pruned records keep
121	  their write-order ordinals for `resume_metrics`. Whole evicted segments
122	  are deleted and only the single boundary segment is rewritten, staged
123	  atomically at `path.trim`; a crash leaves either the old set or a set
124	  pruned to a complete record boundary, and a half-finished trim never
125	  joins recovery. Pruning is serialised with appends, rotations and
126	  compactions, and an unfinished compaction is settled first. Raises
127	  `TypeError` if `quota` is not an integer (booleans do not count),
128	  `ValueError` for a negative quota, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is
129	  missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a
130	  non-string path or a locking/write failure. Old segment sets with no
131	  prune marker need no migration; the first prune starts at zero pruned.
132	- `weighted_batcher.snapshot_metrics(path) -> str` pins the complete
133	  record sequence as of the call and returns a persistable snapshot
134	  handle. The pinned records are copied byte for byte into a
135	  snapshot-private file, so no later append, rotation, compaction or
136	  prune changes what the snapshot reads — the records survive even a
137	  quota-0 prune, and a compaction rewriting the segment members leaves
138	  the creation-time bytes (original newlines, `-0.0`, oversized
139	  counters, key order) untouched. Snapshots are independent of each
140	  other. A crash mid-creation leaves no usable handle behind, and the
141	  orphaned copy is removed transparently by the next write. Raises
142	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
143	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write
144	  failure.
145	- `weighted_batcher.release_metrics(path, handle) -> None` releases a
146	  snapshot handle and deletes its private copy. Reading or releasing the
147	  handle afterwards raises `ValueError`, as does a forged handle or one
148	  belonging to another segment set. Raises `TypeError` if `handle` is
149	  not a string, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing,
150	  `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a non-string
151	  path or a locking/write failure.
152	- `weighted_batcher.resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position=0)`
153	  streams the records pinned for `handle` from `position` onward, with
154	  the same write-order ordinals as `resume_metrics`: records pruned
155	  before the snapshot still occupy their ordinals, a position inside
156	  that pruned region starts at the oldest record the snapshot holds, and
157	  only a position past the creation-time record total (pruned included)
158	  is out of range — equal to the total the stream is empty. Repeated
159	  reads of the same handle always yield the creation-time slice, and
160	  reading never touches the segment-set members, so a member pruned or
161	  compacted away concurrently raises no `FileNotFoundError`. Raises
162	  `TypeError` if `handle` is not a string or `position` is not an
163	  integer (booleans do not count), `ValueError` for a forged, foreign or
164	  released handle and for a negative or out-of-range position (the
165	  latter while iterating), `FileNotFoundError` when neither the log nor
166	  any segment exists, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError`
167	  for a non-string path.
168	
169	## Tests
170	
171	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
172	
173	## Limits
174	
175	The sampler is single-threaded and deterministic per seed.
176	Counters are integers; no floating point rounding is applied to them.
177	No dataset loading and no training loop.
178

## Requirements

## Install

## Run

    python3 -m weighted_batcher --selftest

    python3 -m weighted_batcher record FILE METRICS_JSON
    python3 -m weighted_batcher recover FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher rotate FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher stream FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher compact FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher resume FILE [POSITION]
    python3 -m weighted_batcher prune FILE QUOTA
    python3 -m weighted_batcher snapshot FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher release FILE HANDLE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher snap-resume FILE HANDLE [POSITION]

`rotate` seals `FILE` into a numbered segment (`FILE.1`, then one past the
highest number already present), leaving an empty `FILE` behind, and exits 0.
`compact` merges every segment and the current log into `FILE.1`, leaving an
empty `FILE` behind; an empty log set still produces an empty `FILE.1`.
`resume` prints records from `POSITION` (the number of records already read
from the start in write order, default 0) onward; the position stays valid
across appends, rotations, compactions and pruning. `prune` retains at most
`QUOTA` records, dropping the oldest whole records; `QUOTA` 0 drops every
record. Pruned records keep their write-order positions, so a `POSITION`
inside or at the prune point reads from the oldest surviving record, and
only a position past the total record count (pruned included) is out of
range. `snapshot` pins the complete record sequence at creation time and
prints a persistable handle; `snap-resume` streams the pinned sequence
from `POSITION` (same ordinal rules as `resume`, default 0), and
`release` retires the handle. `rotate`, `stream`, `compact`, `resume`,
`prune`, `snapshot`, `release` and `snap-resume` exit 1 on
failure; wrong argument counts and a `POSITION` or `QUOTA` that is not an
integer print usage on stderr and exit 2.

## Public interface

`weighted_batcher.Sampler(weights, replacement=True, seed=None)`.
- `Sampler.sample(n) -> list[int]` returns drawn indices.
- In without-replacement mode draws accumulate on the instance: repeated
  `sample` calls never return an index already drawn, and requesting more
  draws than the remaining positive-weight items raises `ValueError`.
- `Sampler.weights -> list[float]` as supplied.
- `weighted_batcher.render_metrics(metrics) -> str` returns one line of JSON.
- `weighted_batcher.parse_metrics(line) -> dict` accepts what `render_metrics` produced.
- `weighted_batcher.append_metrics(path, line) -> None` validates one JSON object
  line and appends it to `path`. Concurrent processes appending to the same file
  never interleave records. Raises `OSError` if `line` is not a string or the
  path is not writable, `ValueError` if the top level is not a JSON object, and
  `TypeError` if a key is not a string or a value is not an int or float
  (booleans do not count).
- `weighted_batcher.recover_metrics(path) -> list[dict]` reads the log set
  back: segments `path.1`, `path.2`, ... in ascending order followed by the
  current log at `path`. Every complete newline-terminated line is parsed; a
  torn unterminated tail left by a crashed writer is silently discarded.
  Blank lines (`\n` and `\r\n`) are skipped. A non-JSON complete line raises
  `ValueError` naming its file and line number. An empty or newline-only file
  yields `[]`. Missing files raise `FileNotFoundError` (only when neither the
  current log nor any segment exists); directories raise
  `IsADirectoryError`. Large counters return as exact ints, `-0.0` is
  preserved, and key order follows the file.
- `weighted_batcher.rotate_metrics(path) -> None` seals the current log into
  the next numbered segment (`path.1`, then one past the greatest number
  already present, so a deleted number is never reused) and leaves an empty
  file at `path`; an empty log seals an empty segment. Concurrent appenders
  are serialised with a file lock, so every accepted record lands in exactly
  one segment or in the current log. A crash after sealing but before
  re-creation still leaves the segment readable in write order. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking failure.
- `weighted_batcher.iter_metrics(path)` is the streaming counterpart of
  `recover_metrics`: it yields records line by line across segments and the
  current log without loading them into memory, with the same parsing and
  error semantics.
- `weighted_batcher.compact_metrics(path) -> None` merges all segments and
  the current log into the single fixed segment `path.1` and leaves the
  current log empty; a completely empty set still yields an empty segment.
  Complete records are copied byte for byte with their original newlines —
  not re-rendered, de-duplicated or reordered, so `-0.0`, oversized counters
  and key order are preserved; torn tails are dropped and blank lines
  skipped just like on read. The merge is fully written and flushed to a
  temporary file before being atomically published as `path.compact`, and
  only then are old segments removed and the result renamed to `path.1`;
  a half-written crash leftover never joins recovery, and while staging
  exists recovery and streaming read only it. A later append, rotation or
  compaction transparently finishes an interrupted cleanup. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_metrics(path, position=0)` streams records from
  `position` onward, where `position` is the number of records already read
  from the start of the segment set in write order. The position needs no
  conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
  cleanup, and is only out of range when it exceeds the record total
  (pruned records included); equal to the total the stream is empty.
  Reading stays line by line and linear, never materialising the segment
  set. Raises `TypeError` if `position` is not an integer (booleans do not
  count), `ValueError` for a negative or out-of-range position (the latter
  while iterating), with the same path and line-level errors as
  `iter_metrics`.
- `weighted_batcher.prune_metrics(path, quota)` keeps at most `quota`
  records, dropping whole records from the oldest end in write order;
  `quota` 0 drops every record, and a quota at or above the current count
  removes nothing. A record is never split, empty and torn-tail-only
  segments spend no quota, and survivors keep their bytes, order,
  newlines, `-0.0`, oversized counters and key order. The set remembers
  the number of records pruned (`path.prune`), so pruned records keep
  their write-order ordinals for `resume_metrics`. Whole evicted segments
  are deleted and only the single boundary segment is rewritten, staged
  atomically at `path.trim`; a crash leaves either the old set or a set
  pruned to a complete record boundary, and a half-finished trim never
  joins recovery. Pruning is serialised with appends, rotations and
  compactions, and an unfinished compaction is settled first. Raises
  `TypeError` if `quota` is not an integer (booleans do not count),
  `ValueError` for a negative quota, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is
  missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a
  non-string path or a locking/write failure. Old segment sets with no
  prune marker need no migration; the first prune starts at zero pruned.
- `weighted_batcher.snapshot_metrics(path) -> str` pins the complete
  record sequence as of the call and returns a persistable snapshot
  handle. The pinned records are copied byte for byte into a
  snapshot-private file, so no later append, rotation, compaction or
  prune changes what the snapshot reads — the records survive even a
  quota-0 prune, and a compaction rewriting the segment members leaves
  the creation-time bytes (original newlines, `-0.0`, oversized
  counters, key order) untouched. Snapshots are independent of each
  other. A crash mid-creation leaves no usable handle behind, and the
  orphaned copy is removed transparently by the next write. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write
  failure.
- `weighted_batcher.release_metrics(path, handle) -> None` releases a
  snapshot handle and deletes its private copy. Reading or releasing the
  handle afterwards raises `ValueError`, as does a forged handle or one
  belonging to another segment set. Raises `TypeError` if `handle` is
  not a string, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing,
  `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a non-string
  path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position=0)`
  streams the records pinned for `handle` from `position` onward, with
  the same write-order ordinals as `resume_metrics`: records pruned
  before the snapshot still occupy their ordinals, a position inside
  that pruned region starts at the oldest record the snapshot holds, and
  only a position past the creation-time record total (pruned included)
  is out of range — equal to the total the stream is empty. Repeated
  reads of the same handle always yield the creation-time slice, and
  reading never touches the segment-set members, so a member pruned or
  compacted away concurrently raises no `FileNotFoundError`. Raises
  `TypeError` if `handle` is not a string or `position` is not an
  integer (booleans do not count), `ValueError` for a forged, foreign or
  released handle and for a negative or out-of-range position (the
  latter while iterating), `FileNotFoundError` when neither the log nor
  any segment exists, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError`
  for a non-string path.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

The sampler is single-threaded and deterministic per seed.
Counters are integers; no floating point rounding is applied to them.
No dataset loading and no training loop.

1	"""Durable append-only metric log with rotation, compaction, pruning and resume.
2	
3	Each metric occupies exactly one newline-terminated JSON line.  A record is
4	appended with :func:`os.write` against a single ``O_APPEND`` file
5	descriptor, so concurrent appending processes never interleave one line
6	with another.  Recovery acknowledges only newline-terminated lines: a
7	record torn by a mid-write crash survives as an unterminated tail and is
8	silently discarded.
9	
10	:func:`rotate_metrics` seals the current log into a numbered segment
11	(``path.1``, ``path.2``, ...) and leaves an empty log behind.  Segment
12	numbers are one past the highest number ever used, so deleting a segment
13	from the outside never makes its number come back.  Recovery walks the
14	segments in ascending order followed by the current log, so a record
15	accepted before a rotation never crosses a segment boundary.
16	:func:`iter_metrics` performs the same walk as a line-by-line generator,
17	never loading the segment set into memory.
18	
19	:func:`compact_metrics` merges every segment and the current log into the
20	single fixed segment ``path.1`` and leaves an empty current log.  Records
21	are copied byte for byte, still newline terminated, without re-rendering.
22	The merge lands first in a staging file at ``path.compact``; only after it
23	is fully on disk does cleanup begin.
24	
25	:func:`prune_metrics` enforces a retention quota by dropping whole records
26	from the oldest end.  Evicted records keep their write-order ordinal: the
27	segment set remembers how many records have been pruned in ``path.prune``,
28	and no operation renumbers surviving records.  :func:`resume_metrics`
29	resumes the same write-order walk at an integer read position; the
30	position needs no translation across appends, rotations, compactions,
31	pruning or crash cleanup.
32	
33	:func:`snapshot_metrics` pins the complete record sequence at creation
34	time into a snapshot-private copy (``path.snap.<handle>``) and records the
35	handle in the snapshot registry (``path.snapshots``), so later appends,
36	rotations, compactions and prunes never change what the snapshot reads.
37	:func:`resume_snapshot_metrics` streams a snapshot from a write-order
38	read position with the same ordinal rules as :func:`resume_metrics`, and
39	:func:`release_metrics` retires a handle and its private copy.  A copy
40	left behind by a crash before its handle was registered is not readable
41	and is removed transparently by the next write.
42	
43	:func:`snapshot_diff_metrics` reconciles two snapshots of one segment set
44	in write order -- the handle created first is the old side -- reporting
45	each extra record as ``added``, each vanished one as ``missing`` and each
46	byte-for-byte changed one as ``changed``, one JSON line per difference.
47	:func:`resume_snapshot_delta_metrics` pins the live record boundary the
48	way :func:`snapshot_metrics` pins a snapshot (a brief lock to settle and
49	capture the members, then a lock-free copy) and streams the records past
50	a read position that the holder of an older snapshot handle has not read
51	yet.  A reconciliation is fully lock free, and an incremental pull holds
52	the write lock only for the constant-sized boundary pin -- never while
53	its records are produced -- so appends, rotations, compactions and
54	prunes proceed normally while either read runs.
55	
56	:func:`checkpoint_metrics` persists a reader's place in a caller-named
57	cursor file.  The cursor binds the write-order read position, the
58	snapshot handle the reader pulls through and that snapshot's record
59	boundary (its pruned count and record total); every advance replaces the
60	whole cursor atomically, so a crash between consuming and advancing
61	leaves either the old cursor or the new one, never a half-written file.
62	:func:`resume_checkpoint_metrics` reads that one file and streams the
63	pinned snapshot from the stored position with exactly the ordinal rules
64	of :func:`resume_snapshot_metrics`.  A cursor takes no log lock to write
65	and reads only the snapshot's private copy, so concurrent readers with
66	separate cursor files and same-process writers neither block nor lose
67	updates.
68	
69	:func:`checkpoint_group_metrics` advances a whole group of such cursors
70	in one commit.  It publishes a single unified commit record
71	(``path.groupcursor``) covering every cursor in the group -- one write
72	for the whole group instead of one per reader -- and only then replaces
73	the individual cursor files, so a crash leaves either the pre-commit
74	cursors or, once the next group commit finishes the published plan, the
75	post-commit ones, never a durable mixture.  Concurrent group commits
76	are serialised by a lock anchored on ``path.groupcursor.lock`` -- never
77	on the log -- so same-process readers and writers neither deadlock
78	against a group commit nor report spurious locking failures.
79	
80	:func:`replay_metrics` re-reads a window of the write-order record
81	sequence, merging the cursor's pinned snapshot copy with a pinned live
82	boundary and de-duplicating by write ordinal, so a record already
83	consumed inside the window is never produced twice.  A window start
84	inside the pruned region backfills from the oldest surviving record and
85	reports the gap; a window end past the record total (pruned records
86	included) closes with a gap.  The live side is pinned the way
87	:func:`resume_snapshot_delta_metrics` pins it, so pruning, rotation and
88	compaction proceed concurrently and the read never holds the write lock
89	while records are produced.
90	
91	Every data-file descriptor is released before a rename on platforms that
92	cannot rename open files (Windows), so sealing, compaction and pruning no
93	longer raise ``PermissionError`` there.

172	def _segment_numbers(path):

176	    ``path.trim`` and their temporaries) is deliberately invisible here.

214	def _same_inode(fd, path):

413	    handle leaves the copy unnamed by the registry; such a half-finished
414	    handle never participates in reads, and its copy is deleted here by
415	    the next write.  Copies of live handles are always kept, so a prune

439	def _finish_staged_prune(path):

443	    by any append, rotation or compaction that finds a plan a crashed
444	    prune left behind.  The plan is the commit point: the trimmed boundary
445	    segment has already landed whole at ``path.trim``, so finishing is
446	    pure filesystem cleanup -- delete the evicted members, publish the
447	    trimmed boundary atomically, then finalise the marker to the pruned
448	    count.  Lock-free readers reconcile a half-finished plan themselves in
449	    :func:`_resolve_members`, so a crash at any point exposes either the
450	    old segment set or the fully pruned one, never a mixture.
451	    """

460	    if plan is None:

466	        _unlink_if_exists(_label_member(label, path))

474	        # caller's lock fd is allowed to dangle on the replaced inode.

483	    observations bracket a window in which no prune committed, so the
484	    directory listing taken between them belongs to that marker's world.

492	        while True:
493	            chunk = os.read(fd, _READ_CHUNK)

502	def _resolve_members(path):
503	    """Pick the member files and pruned count to read.
504	
505	    Returns ``(members, pruned)``.  Numbered segments come first in
506	    ascending order, followed by the current log when it exists; the
507	    pruned count is the number of records already gone from the oldest
508	    end.
509	
510	    Resolution is lock-free but crash- and commit-consistent: the prune
511	    marker is read before and after the directory is listed and the pair
512	    must match, otherwise a commit straddled the listing and the read
513	    resolves again.  Pruning commits in the order plan publication,
514	    filesystem cleanup, marker finalisation, so an unchanged marker
515	    brackets a directory state that marker reconciles to exactly one
516	    settled record sequence:
517	
518	    * A compaction's fully landed ``path.compact`` staging file, while
519	      present, alone is the segment set.
520	    * A pending prune plan: evicted members still on disk are ignored,
521	      and while the trimmed boundary waits at ``path.trim`` it stands in
522	      for the boundary member; once the boundary is published its staging
523	      name is gone and the finished member is read directly.
524	    """
525	    members = pruned = None
526	    before = _marker_observation(path)
527	    for _ in range(1000):
528	        members, pruned, after = _resolve_once(path, before)
529	        if after == before:
530	            return members, pruned
531	        before = after
532	    # Extremely contended: return the last self-consistent pair rather
533	    # than loop forever; the data it reads is itself whole.
534	    return members, pruned

543	            else (int(data), None)

554	        ]

580	def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
581	    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.
582	
583	    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
584	    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
585	    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
586	    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
587	    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
588	    """
589	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
590	    pending = b""
591	    lineno = 0
592	    try:
593	        while True:
594	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
595	            if not chunk:
596	                break
597	            pending += chunk
598	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
599	            for raw in complete:
600	                lineno += 1
601	                yield lineno, raw
602	    finally:
603	        os.close(fd)

610	            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
611	            continue
612	        try:
613	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
614	            yield parse_metrics(text)
615	        except ValueError as exc:
616	            raise ValueError(
617	                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
618	            ) from exc

626	def iter_metrics(path):
627	    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.
628	
629	    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
630	    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
631	    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
632	    a single line may be arbitrarily long.

635	    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
636	    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
637	    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.  A pending prune
638	    is reconciled the same way: only surviving records are yielded.
639

641	    a segment holding only a torn tail yields nothing.  Blank empty lines
642	    (``\\n``) and CRLF blank lines (``\\r\\n``) are skipped.  Any other
643	    complete line that is not a metrics JSON object raises
644	    :class:`ValueError` naming the file and its 1-based line number.

646	    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
647	    content problems are reported lazily as the offending line is reached.
648

650	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
651	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
652	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
653	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics JSON
654	            object (raised while iterating).

656	    if not isinstance(path, str):
657	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")

659	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")

662	    if not members:
663	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")

665	    def _generate():

687	def _iter_raw_file_records(copy_path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
688	    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.

690	    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
691	    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
692	    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
693	    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
694	    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives untouched.
695	    """

697	    pending = b""

700	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
701	            if not chunk:
702	                break
703	            pending += chunk
704	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
705	            for raw in complete:
706	                if raw and raw != b"\r":
707	                    yield raw + b"\n"
708	    finally:
709	        os.close(fd)

771	def rotate_metrics(path):
772	    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.
773	
774	    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
775	    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
776	    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number
777	    back out; an empty log seals an empty segment.  Afterwards ``path``
778	    exists again as an empty file ready for appending.  Every record
779	    acknowledged by a write ends up either wholly in a segment or wholly
780	    in the current log, never split across two.
781	
782	    A crash after the rename but before the live file is recreated still
783	    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the
784	    live log.
785	
786	    Raises:
787	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
788	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
789	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, locking fails, or another OS
790	            error occurs while sealing.  Nothing is written when locking
791	            fails.
792	    """
793	    if not isinstance(path, str):
794	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
795	    if os.path.isdir(path):
796	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
797	
798	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
799	    try:
800	        _finish_pending(path)
801	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
802	        used = _segment_numbers(path)
803	        number = (max(used) + 1) if used else 1
804	        segment = f"{path}.{number}"
805	        # POSIX: the rename happens while the lock fd is held (an open
806	        # file may be renamed); the lock makes appenders reopen the path
807	        # before writing.  Windows has no fd in hand at all, so the
808	        # PermissionError an open live log used to cause cannot happen.
809	        os.rename(path, segment)

811	        # won the unlocked rename window on a lock-less platform may have
812	        # landed a record there first, and it belongs in the current log.
813	        new_fd = os.open(
814	            path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
815	        )
816	        os.close(new_fd)
817	    finally:
818	        if fd is not None:
819	            os.close(fd)

879	def compact_metrics(path):
880	    """Merge every segment and the current log into one segment.
881	
882	    All records are copied into the fixed segment ``path.1`` in write
883	    order; the current log is left empty afterwards.  Records move byte
884	    for byte with their original newlines -- nothing is re-rendered,
885	    de-duplicated or reordered, so ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key
886	    order are all preserved.  Residual torn lines are not records and
887	    are dropped; blank lines are skipped as on read; overlong single
888	    lines move as-is.  A completely empty set still produces an empty
889	    ``path.1``.
890	
891	    The merge is first written to a private temporary file and only
892	    renamed onto ``path.compact`` after the whole file has landed and
893	    been flushed (its descriptor already closed, so the rename also
894	    works on Windows), so that name always holds a complete whole
895	    segment: a half-written file left by a crash never joins recovery
896	    and never affects reads.  Once staged, recovery and streaming read
897	    only that segment; cleanup publishes it as ``path.1``, removes the
898	    other numbered segments and empties the current log.  An interrupted
899	    cleanup is finished transparently by the next append, rotation,
900	    compaction or prune.  The pruned-record count stored by earlier
901	    prunes is left untouched.
902	
903	    Raises:
904	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
905	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
906	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing the
907	            merged segment fails.  A failed write removes the private
908	            temporary file and leaves the segment set untouched.
909	    """
910	    if not isinstance(path, str):
911	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
912	    if os.path.isdir(path):
913	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
914	
915	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
916	    try:
917	        # A previous compaction may have staged its segment and died
918	        # before cleanup; settle that world before merging again.  So may
919	        # a previous prune.
920	        _finish_pending(path)
921	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
922	
923	        staging = _staging_path(path)
924	        tmp = staging + ".tmp"
925	        try:
926	            out = os.open(
927	                tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666
928	            )

930	                for member in _segment_members(path):
931	                    for raw in _iter_raw_records(member):

950	        if fd is not None:

985	    removed, and ``quota`` 0 drops every record.  Records are dropped in

987	    record is never split.  Empty segments and segments holding only a
988	    torn tail spend no quota and are removed with the prefix ahead of
989	    them.  Surviving records move byte for byte: order, original
990	    newlines, ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key order are unchanged,
991	    and an overlong single line still counts as exactly one record.

994	    the total number pruned, so read positions never shift (see
995	    :func:`resume_metrics`).  Whole evicted segments are deleted; only
996	    the single segment the cut lands inside is rewritten, via a
997	    ``path.trim`` staging file and a JSON plan in ``path.prune``, so a
998	    crash leaves either the old set or a set pruned to a complete record
999	    boundary -- a half-finished trim never joins recovery.  Pruning is
1000	    serialised with appends, rotations and compactions by the live-log
1001	    lock, and an unfinished compaction is settled first; every accepted
1002	    record is therefore either kept or dropped, never lost or duplicated.

1010	            truncated segment fails.

1016	            f"retention quota must be an integer, got {type(quota).__name__}"
1017	        )

1022

1024	    try:
1025	        _finish_pending(path)
1026	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
1027

1029	        # One streaming count pass (the same cheap line walk reads use)
